title: Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones II
statement:
You get a matrix `grid` whose cells hold `0` or `1`. Draw exactly three rectangles along the grid lines, each made of whole cells and containing at least one cell, so that no cell lies in two of them; rectangles may share a border. Every cell holding a `1` must end up inside one of the three rectangles.

Return the smallest possible sum of the three rectangles' areas. The grid always contains at least three `1`s.
notes:
## Intuition

Three non-overlapping rectangles can always be separated by straight cuts: one line across the whole grid puts one rectangle on one side and two on the other, and a second line across that side separates the two. That leaves six layouts: three horizontal bands, three vertical bands, or one half kept whole while the opposite half is split by a perpendicular cut (four ways). Inside a block the cheapest rectangle is the bounding box of its `1`s, so trying every cut position of every layout finds the optimum, far faster than trying all triples of rectangles.

## Approach

1. `cover(top, bottom, left, right)` returns the bounding-box area of a block's `1`s, or `0` if it has none.
2. A half depends on one cut only, so compute `topHalf[i]`, `bottomHalf[i]` (cut below row `i`) and `leftHalf[j]`, `rightHalf[j]` (cut right of column `j`) once.
3. For every pair of horizontal cuts `i < j`, add the top half, the middle band and the bottom half; likewise for vertical cuts.
4. For every horizontal cut `i` and vertical cut `j`, measure the four corners; each L-layout is one whole half plus the two corners opposite it.
5. Keep the smallest total in `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid = [[1,0,1],[1,1,1]]` gives `topHalf = [3]`, `bottomHalf = [3]`, `leftHalf = [2, 4]` and `rightHalf = [4, 2]`. Two rows allow no stacked bands. The vertical cuts after columns 0 and 1 cost `2 + 1 + 2 = 5`. For `i = 0, j = 0` the corners are `1, 1, 1, 2` and the L-layouts cost `6, 5, 5, 6`; `j = 1` gives `6, 5, 6, 5`. The answer is `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n·(m² + n² + m·n)): O(m² + n² + m·n) cut choices, each scanning at most the whole grid once.
- Space: O(m + n) for the arrays of halves.

## Pitfalls

- Bands alone are not enough: example 2 needs the whole top row plus a bottom row split in two.
- A block without `1`s adds `0`. That never undercuts the answer: with at least three `1`s, some rectangle holds two of them and can be split between them at no extra cost.
- Every block needs at least one row and column, so cuts stop before the last row and column.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cover` | bounding-box area of the `1`s in one block |
| `topHalf[i]`, `bottomHalf[i]` | covers above and below a cut under row `i` |
| `leftHalf[j]`, `rightHalf[j]` | covers left and right of a cut after column `j` |
| `i`, `j` | cut positions |
| `topLeft` ... `bottomRight` | covers of the four corners of cuts `i` and `j` |
| `best` | smallest total found so far |

narration.6: cover measures one block of the grid: the area of the tightest rectangle around its 1s.
narration.8: Scan every cell of the block, row by row.
narration.10: Each 1 may stretch the bounding box in any direction.
narration.18: A block without 1s needs no rectangle; otherwise the area is height times width.
narration.24: A half depends on one cut only, so its cover is computed once and reused.
narration.26: Cover of everything above a cut just below row i.
narration.27: Cover of everything below that cut.
narration.30: Cover of everything left of a cut just right of column j.
narration.31: Cover of everything right of that cut.
narration.36: Two horizontal cuts, below rows i and j, make three stacked bands.
narration.38: Top half, the middle band between the cuts, and the bottom half.
narration.42: Two vertical cuts, right of columns i and j, make three side-by-side bands.
narration.44: Left half, the middle band, and the right half.
narration.48: One horizontal cut i and one vertical cut j split the grid into four corners.
narration.50: Cover of the top-left corner; the next lines measure the other three.
narration.54: Keep the top half whole and split the bottom, or keep the bottom whole and split the top.
narration.55: Keep the left half whole and split the right, or keep the right whole and split the left.
narration.58: best holds the cheapest of all layouts.
